newsitem.title: USA: Hermes Europe Railtel BV to sell $175 mln in debt.
newsitem.headline: Hermes Europe Railtel BV to sell $175 mln in debt.

text.p: Hermes Europe Railtel BV, a company building a pan-European fiber-optic telephone network, plans to sell $175 million in junk bonds over the next several weeks in the U.S. and Europe, according to a confidential prospectus, a copy of which was obtained by Reuters.

Proceeds from the offering will be used to build a 17,000 kilometer high-capacity fiber-optic network designed to interconnect a majority of the largest western and central European cities, according to the document.
Market sources said once the network is built, Hermes plans to sell telephone capacity in bulk to other carriers.
Hermes is 86 percent owned by Global TeleSystems Group Inc, a private U.S. company whose major shareholders include hedge fund manager George Soros.
The remaining 14 percent stake in Hermes is owned by Hit Rail B.V., a consortium of eleven European railroad companies.
Market sources said the railway companies plan to allow Hermes to lay fiber-optic cable alongside their railroad lines.
The offering will consist of $175 million in senior notes due 2007, according to the prospectus. The structure of the securities will include a two-year prefunded interest reserve.

Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette, UBS Securities and Lehman Brothers will underwrite the offering. The roadshow for the deal will begin in Europe this week and continue in the U.S. next week, sources said.

"This is the QWest of Europe," said one market source, referring to Qwest Communications International Inc, a company building a fiber-optic network in the U.S., which sold $250 million in junk bonds earlier this year.
"The difference is that QWest is the sixth company to build a fiber-optic network in the U.S. Hermes will be the first in Europe," he said.
